newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Anti-paedophile campaigner attacked in Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Anti-paedophile campaigner attacked in Belgium.

text.p: A prominent anti-paedophile campaigner in Belgium said an unidentified attacker tried to strangle her as she returned home late on Wednesday night, warning her she would be killed if she continued her activities.
Marie-France Botte, a surgical collar round her neck, told Belgian television she had been attacked and threatened as she returned to her third-floor apartment.
"A man who I couldn't identify attacked me from behind and tried to strangle me. I was very lucky to escape," she said, adding that there had been no attempt to rob her.
"He told me I would pay. That he would kill me," she said.
Her office said she had reported the attack to the police. A police spokesman could not immediately confirm the report, but pointed out that the papers could still be being processed.

Operation Marie-France Botte, an organisation dedicated to stamping out paedophilia around the globe, has had offices in Bangkok, Phnom Penh and Sarajevo for the past 10 years. It opened its office in Brussels 18 months ago.
Belgium has been in shock since mid-August after the unveiling of a paedophile kidnap, sexual abuse and murder gang led by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux.
So far the bodies of four young girls have been found, two other girls have been rescued from a secret dungeon and police are searching for at least seven other missing children.
A total of 13 people have been arrested in the affair that has sent shockwaves across Europe.
